title: Interventional Equivalence of Context-Specific Staged Trees under Swap and Resize Moves
banked_reason: terminal:laundering — the delivered theorem proves incompleteness of a custom whole-level grammar while the frozen topic requires a complete target-preserving move calculus and terminating equivalence procedure; the run expressly disclaims the promised result.
gap_reasons: The delivered central theorem proves incompleteness of a newly specified whole-level grammar, whereas the recorded topic promises a complete target-preserving move calculus with a terminating equivalence procedure.
The core itself expressly disclaims completeness of any enlarged calculus.
The missing faithful fix is the original unsolved global theorem, not a local D0.5 repair.
proof_attempt_summary: The run attempted to derive a complete synchronized swap/resize calculus for equal coupled interventional staged-tree models. It instead proved an honest infinite family of equal-image, same-target counterexamples showing that a custom three-rule whole-level grammar is incomplete, including examples inside compatible CS-complete interventional CStrees. What remains is the original global task: define a larger sound grammar and prove its completeness and terminating equivalence procedure under overlapping stages, active slots, and multiple regimes.
tldr: An analytic family of finite-alphabet interventions gives equal labelled positive models and identical physical root targets in two CS-complete interventional CStrees that are isolated under the custom whole-level swap/resize grammar. Exact cross-regime equations and rank-one minors certify equality; a contextwise mixed swap transports the pair. Finite search decides grammar connectivity and certifies equality when it finds a path.
gap: Existing observational swap/resize completeness and interventional equality tests do not establish connectivity under local rewrites that keep the same external target footprint. Raw image equality can even identify different menus when no baseline anchors a singleton stage.
fill: Test and characterize completeness of the explicit finite grammar inside each fixed-target fiber; if it fails, certify a same-target disconnected pair and derive a sound structural enlargement. Use exact conditional-sharing equations for independent endpoint audits and rational separation.
